pairs.why: A's pi pattern is a darker orange, tone-on-tone and quiet like the real card, while B's pi glyphs are larger and higher-contrast on a bright glow, so they compete with the hero.
B is a close, central view of a few big quiet shapes (posts, deck, ring) like the real card, while A pulls back to a tiny pier in a busy field of water caustics.
Both put the hat on a plain concentric-ring field with no props, so staging gives no reason to choose.
B's warm, saturated, lit scene with a few readable props is closer to the real cards' lively environments than A's dull grey moonscape, but both keep the hero central and load is similar.
A keeps the bottle on a plain sunburst like the real card, while B adds water droplets that the real card doesn't have.
A uses only hedge, lawn and a curved path like the real card, while B adds a bench, flower pot, lantern and corner bushes that crowd the scene.
A's sand has a few larger pebbles like the real card's two stones, while B scatters many tiny pebbles and gives the duck an open smiling mouth that the real card lacks.
Both show the same tree, path, bushes and tiny flowers around a central table, so environment load is equally close to the real card.
